result.summary: The new setting is persisted but cannot be edited in the UI and does not control shutdown behavior.

findings.title: Connect the saved timeout to the shutdown drain
findings.body: Posting shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 now saves that value successfully, but shutdown still uses _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT at scheduler.py:635. That constant reads only the environment at import time, defaulting to 60 seconds. With no environment override, the newly accepted setting therefore cannot extend the drain; resources are still closed after 60 seconds.
findings.recommendation: Read the current settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout when shutdown begins, preserving the intended environment override, and test that a saved value controls the actual drain.

findings.title: Add the missing settings form input
findings.body: The new template context value is never consumed: settings.html contains no shutdown_drain_timeout input. Users cannot view or change this setting, and every browser save submits no value, causing line 550 to persist 60.0 even after a custom value was saved through a direct POST. The existing test_settings_page_renders_new_config_fields assertion also expects this missing input.
findings.recommendation: Add a numeric input associated with settings-form, populated from shutdown_drain_timeout and supporting fractional values within the accepted bounds. Verify a browser form round trip preserves 120.5.

next_steps: Complete the template and shutdown integration, then run the settings and shutdown tests.
